# The Value of Disagreement: Why the Best Meetings Don't End in Consensus

There is a common picture of what a successful meeting looks like. Everyone files into a conference room—or these days, joins a video call—and after some discussion, the group converges on a shared conclusion. Nods all around. Someone volunteers to write up the summary. The meeting ends early, even. By this measure, harmony equals success, and friction equals failure.

But this picture deserves a second look. Agreement, it turns out, can be deceptive. Sometimes everyone nods because they genuinely share a view. But sometimes they nod because the discussion was too vague to expose the differences between them, or because nobody wanted to be the one to object, or because each person walked out with a private, slightly different understanding of what was agreed. The meeting *looked* harmonious, but the disagreement didn't disappear. It simply went underground, where it will resurface later—usually at a worse moment, like when a product ships or a budget gets spent.
